Kasturba Hospital Observes the World Breastfeeding Week 2025
Monday, 11 August 2025
1586 Hits
Kasturba Hospital celebrated the
World Breastfeeding Week 2025
from August 1 to 7, reaffirming the importance of breastfeeding for the health of babies, mothers, and society at large.
Observed annually in the first week of August, World Breastfeeding Week is coordinated by the World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action (WABA) in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF. Launched in 1992, this global campaign promotes awareness about the life-long physical, mental, and economic benefits of breastfeeding. This year’s theme,
“Prioritize Breastfeeding: Build Sustainable Support Systems”
, underlines the urgent need for strong, equitable, and long-term structures that empower breastfeeding mothers.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr Poonam Shivkumar Verma (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital) said, “Breastfeeding is far more than a feeding method—it is a nurturing bond that ensures unparalleled nutrition and protection for the baby, supporting early brain development, emotional connection, and long-term health.
“Breast milk provides the ideal nutrition and immunity boost for infants, helping them achieve developmental milestones with a stronger foundation for cognitive and physical growth,” Dr Suchi Jain (Head, Obstetrics & Gynaecology Department) stated. “However, we must acknowledge that breastfeeding, though natural, is not always easy. New mothers often face physical discomfort, emotional challenges, and societal barriers that require consistent guidance and reassurance.”
During the week-long observance, Kasturba Hospital conducted interactive awareness sessions for expectant and new mothers, highlighting best practices in breastfeeding, the role of family and community support, and ways to overcome common challenges. Lactation counselling services, one-on-one guidance, and demonstration workshops were organized, ensuring personalized assistance for mothers. Educational materials were distributed in local languages to reach rural and semi-urban communities.
